name: Cinematic teal and orange
summary: A staged, shallow-focus frame with warm orange skin against cool teal shadows, graded like a film still. It is a colour recipe from the digital intermediate, and it is now a default look of films, ads and image prompts.

philosophy.core_thesis: Two opposed hues, the warm skin and the cool environment, give a frame instant depth and a sense of cinema.
design_principles: Light with a warm key at 3200 to 3500K and a cool fill or ambient at 5600 to 6500K, at a key-to-fill ratio of 4:1.
Shoot at 35 to 85mm (35mm format), f/1.8 to f/2.8, so the subject separates from the background by at least 2 stops of blur.
Grade the shadows to teal (hue 185° to 195°) and the skin and highlights to orange (hue 20° to 30°).
Reduce the other hues by 20 to 40% in saturation, so that the pair carries the image.
Frame at 2.39:1 or 16:9 with a subject on a third line and negative space with a leading line.
Add atmosphere: haze, backlight, practical lights and a vignette of −15%.
anti_patterns: Even, neutral white balance on skin and shadow
Saturated greens, magentas and yellows that compete with the pair
Flat front light and a deep-focus background
Casual snapshot framing with no staging
Teal skin or orange sky from a heavy-handed hue shift
A uniform tint over the whole frame, with no separation

composition.framing: A wide 2.39:1 or 16:9 frame with a controlled foreground and background.
composition.viewpoint: Eye level or slightly low, at 2 to 5m, with a lens of 35 to 85mm.
composition.geometry: Leading lines, a rim light and layered depth: foreground blur, subject, lit background.
composition.subject_placement: On a third line with look space; the subject takes 20–40% of the frame.

light.quality: Controlled: a soft or semi-hard key, practicals and a haze that shows beams.
light.direction: Three-quarter key from the side, rim light from behind, cool fill from the opposite side.
light.time_of_day: Golden hour, blue hour or a lit night set

lens_and_camera.focus: Focus pulled to the eyes; the background falls into blur with oval bokeh from an anamorphic lens if used.

colour_and_grade.treatment: Complementary split: orange skin and highlights against teal shadows and background, with other hues pulled down.
grade_recipe: Set the black point at 4% and a soft shoulder at 92% in a log or flat base.
Add an S-curve of +25% contrast around the midpoint of 18% grey.
Push shadows toward teal: hue 190°, saturation +30%, strength 35%.
Push highlights and skin toward orange: hue 25°, saturation +20%, strength 30%.
Lower the saturation of greens and magentas by −30% and of yellows by −20%.
Add a vignette of −15%, a halation glow at 8% and a 2.39:1 crop.

subject_and_staging.staging: The scene is designed: costume, set colour and practical lights are chosen to land in the teal or orange family.
subject_and_staging.direction: Posed with intent: a look off camera, a lit profile or a slow walk; the pose reads as a still from a story.

workflow: Shoot flat or in log with a neutral white balance.
Build a primary grade: exposure, contrast and white point.
Add the split: teal in the shadows and orange in the highlights with a hue-versus-hue curve.
Use a skin-tone qualifier to keep faces at hue 20°–30°.
Add halation, grain and a vignette, then crop to 2.39:1.
post_processing.output: A 2.39:1 still or a 16:9 frame in Rec. 709, with a look that holds when it is resized for a poster.

positive: warm key light and cool fill

canonical_works.work: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl

emotion.target_response: Drama and scale: the viewer feels a story and a hero in a cool, large world.

avoid_when: The brief needs documentary honesty or accurate product colour.
The look is already a cliché for the audience and a fresh grade is wanted.

modifiers.how: Remove the split toning, set white balance at 5500K and shoot at f/8; keep the saturation of the colour and the deep focus.
Replace the lit set with one on-camera flash at 8:1, drop the shallow focus and the vignette; keep the warm skin.

sources.title: Steve Hullfish, The Art and Technique of Digital Color Correction (Focal Press, 2nd ed., 2012)
